Abstract excerpt: Micro-actions are subtle, short, low-amplitude body movements, such as a fidgeting hand or a slight head tilt, that humans perform with little conscious intent yet that reliably leak emotional and psychological state. Understanding them goes beyond assigning a label: a model must also describe which body parts move and reason, faithfully, about why a clip warrants a particular fine-grained category.
